title: Subvocalization: why silent reading isn't silent
caption:
You're never truly silent when you read.
A guy reads a bus ad in his head, then feels his throat buzzing with tiny movements.
It's subvocalization: your brain sends speech signals to your vocal cords even in silence.
Try it now - did your throat move while reading this?
